summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to ₹78.5 crore and EBITDA rose 52% to ₹15.1 crore, with margin at 19.2%.
summary.overview: Maharaja & Speedex reported H1 FY27 (first earnings call after listing): revenue from operations of ₹78.5 crore (up 36% YoY), EBITDA of ₹15.1 crore (up 52%, margin 19.2% vs 17.2%) and PAT of ₹9.9 crore (up 50%). Gross margin expanded about 447 bps sequentially, helped by lower outsourcing, a richer mix of value-added products and an ~8% price increase. Capacity stands at 72 lakh bottles per year after internal-accrual additions, with a 31 lakh unit IPO-funded expansion due in Q4 FY27 taking it to ~103 lakh. Short-term borrowings of ~₹22.7 crore were fully repaid and D/E is 0.04.

financial_highlights.change: +36% YoY; +21% over H2 FY26 as stated
management attributed to lower outsourcing, mix and price increase

financial_highlights.metric: Employee cost as % of sales (6 months)

segments.name: OEM/ODM (B2B)
segments.commentary: Roughly 53-55% of revenue; serves more than 50 OEM/ODM customers with no single customer above ~10-10.5%. Management targets reducing this share to ~35% over 2-3 years. Contribution to H1 EBITDA margin cited as ~18%.

segments.name: Own brand - distributor network
segments.commentary: About 100 distributors currently, targeting more than 150 by end of FY27. Majority of own-brand sales come via dealers. Own-brand EBITDA margin cited as ~20% in H1, with a stated 2.5-3% premium to OEM margin.

segments.name: Online (B2C)
segments.commentary: Share of business rose from ~10% last year to 14.5% now, targeting 20-22% by end-CY26 and ~30% by end of next year. Present on Amazon, Flipkart and Blinkit; EBITDA margin cited at ~21% in H1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at more than 45% (management cited 45-48%), with H2 expected to be stronger than H1.
Medium-term ambition: capacity growth of 40-50% per year and revenue growth of at least 50%, described as ballpark.
EBITDA margin expected to stay around 19-19.5% long-term; extra margin to be reinvested in brand marketing.
Expansion to ~103 lakh units/year expected to go live in Q4 FY27 (IPO-funded 31 lakh units).
Market share target of 10% by about FY31 from ~2% currently.
New lines take about 4-5 months to install and ramp to 85-90% efficiency in about 2 months.
Backward-looking revenue potential: new lines ~₹23-24 crore per month, existing 62 lakh base ~₹180-190 crore per year (per management).
Working capital inventory days not expected above 90 days; no further funding needed for ~50% growth, but funding may be needed for ~100% growth.
Plans to launch back-to-school hydration SKUs and bento/tiffin boxes (via trading) in H2; manufacturing of tiffin boxes only once above ~5% of revenue, potentially H2 FY28.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 72 lakh bottles/year after internal-accrual additions (earlier base ~62.82 lakh); Feb-2026 lines reached 90% efficiency by May and 95% currently.
IPO-funded 31 lakh unit expansion to go live in Q4 FY27, taking total to ~103 lakh units/year.
Further expansion of 30-40% on current land feasible with minor modifications; additional funding ~₹20-25 crore, with a firmer figure expected around end of CY26.
Management adds new lines once existing capacity reaches 85-90% efficiency; each line takes 4-5 months.
Shifted all capacity to a new facility in Q1 to secure land for the next couple of years; some outsourced items now insourced (outsourcing reduced to 6.5% from 11-12%).
demand_pricing: Management described the market as supply-constrained; Chinese imports made costlier by ~20-25% due to anti-dumping duties, BIS norms, and higher USD and freight costs.
Price increase of ~8% taken in the market during the period amid the war-related cost turmoil.
Product mix shift: value-added and novelty products rose to more than 23% of mix from ~19%.
Share of OEM/ODM customers' wallet: 15-40% of a brand's requirements for legacy players, 100% for some online-focused brands; management says concentration is a choice.
Management noted that rivals (Cello, Borosil) added capacity but argued scale, SKU breadth (200+ SKUs, 5 design patents) and the 30-40k piece run economics are hard to replicate.

qa_highlights.question: Blended capacity utilisation in H1 FY27 and revenue potential post expansion to 103 lakh units?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a blended utilisation figure; existing lines at ~40-45 lakh were run from April and 15-16 lakh new capacity from May. New lines add ~₹23-24 crore revenue; the 62 lakh base could deliver ~₹180-190 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of ~447 bps sequential gross margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower outsourcing (6.5% vs 11-12%), higher value-added mix (23%+ vs 19%), ~8% price increase, and in-house printing/coloring/polishing saving ~1.5% of gross margin. Rejection rate also reduced.

qa_highlights.question: Market share and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently ~2% share, targeting 10% in ~6 years. Legacy importers now run 20-25 SKUs versus 200+ earlier; management sees supply as constrained.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 40-50% growth target for capacity or revenue, and is 45-50% revenue growth achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity target ~40% a year, revenue at least 50% (ballpark). Management is 'very confident' of more than 45% revenue growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Mix between OEM/ODM and own brand, and whether online growth continues?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM/ODM ~54-55%; target own brand ~65% in 3-4 years; online up from 10% to 14.5% and targeted at 20-22% by year-end and ~30% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise to ~8.75% of sales, and H1 vs H2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Hiring in progress; cost ratio expected to stabilise near current levels with ~0.5% further increase in marketing headcount. Management said there is no seasonality in the trade, and H1 growth was held back by plant shifting and ramp delays.

risks_watch: Ramp-up risk: new lines took about two months to reach 85-90% efficiency and H1 growth was affected by plant relocation.
Employee cost rose to ~8.75% of sales in six months from ~7.25%; monitor if the stated stabilisation holds.
Customer concentration within OEM/ODM (up to ~10-10.5% per customer) and dependence on large OEM/ODM buyers wanting 30-50% of capacity.
Working capital: inventory days ~90 and receivables 45-55 days; further funding needed if growth reaches ~100%.
Policy dependence: benefits rest on BIS norms and anti-dumping duties; import substitution from non-duty countries is limited so far.
Execution on the Q4 FY27 expansion and on online/distributor scale-up (150+ distributors, 20-22% online share by year-end).
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and capacity, with a clear 40-50% capacity and 45%+ revenue ambition. Answers were more hedged on specifics like the blended utilisation figure, the incremental capex estimate and margin expansion, which were described as ballpark or "around" figures.

Analysts pushed on employee cost rising to ~8.75% of sales, H1 vs H2 seasonalit

quality.why: H1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to ₹78.5 crore, helped by an ~8% price increase, a richer value-added mix (23%+ vs 19%) and capacity additions, with no one-off gains, losses or low-base effects flagged in the brief; the 36% trails management's 45% target, which the brief attributes to plant relocation and ramp-up delays rather than a one-off.
